candidate.blueprint_topic: Basic Care and Comfort — newborn circumcision aftercare
candidate.educational_objective: Teach routine circumcision-site hygiene and friction protection while helping parents distinguish expected healing from bleeding or infection signs that require evaluation.

options.A: Keep the area clean, use petroleum jelly/dressing as instructed to prevent sticking, and report more than minor bleeding or signs of infection
options.B: Scrub the incision with alcohol at every diaper change to prevent infection
options.C: Avoid changing the diaper for 24 hours so the incision is not disturbed
options.D: Treat spreading redness, pus, or persistent bleeding as expected normal healing

candidate.rationale: AAP parent guidance recommends keeping the circumcision site clean and commonly using petroleum jelly with the dressing or on the healing surface to prevent sticking and friction. Mild redness/yellow healing material can be normal, but more than minor bleeding, spreading redness, pus, marked swelling, or other concerning findings warrant medical evaluation. Alcohol scrubbing and delayed diaper changes are not routine care. Therefore A is the best answer.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Post-circumcision care centers on gentle cleanliness, petroleum jelly/dressing as instructed, and recognition of abnormal bleeding or infection signs.
